newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower -trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower -trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by projections for strong packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Cash hog prices started Wednesday weak but turned firmer amid ideas that higher pork prices at midday signaled that pork demand had improved, they said.

Support also was expected from forecasts for a spring snowstorm Thursday and Friday in the western Corn Belt. The storm could make for difficult marketings by causing slick country roads and reducing visibility, dealers said.

Total accumulation by Friday could be close to six inches from eastern Nebraska through most of Iowa, along with central Illinois and Indiana, according to Weather Express 48 hour precipitation forecast maps.

At midday, prices on hams weighing 20 to 26 lbs were quoted $1.00 per cwt higher while pork bellies were quoted steady to $1.00 higher, USDA reported. There were 44.25 loads of pork cuts sold and 13.0 loads of trimmed/processed pork sold, USDA said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants could range $53.00 to $53.50 dollars.
Illinois tops were seen at $52.50 to $53.00 and Indiana/Ohio hogs could range $52.00 to $52.50, sources in those areas said.
